about: The Lego Mindstorms exercise is the opening Part IA coursework activity, with 5 timetabled sessions in Michaelmas; the department's preparation page (last updated 2022, so possibly out of date) places it from Thursday of Week 1 to Thursday of Week 2. In teams, students design, build and program in Python a Lego system that demonstrates some aspect of engineering science, then present it in the final session, with prizes for the best systems. It carries 12 coursework marks (4 sessions at 2 marks plus an assessment out of 4), with a qualifying level of 10 (2026-27 credit notice).

notes.h: What the Lego Mindstorms exercise is
notes.body:
The Lego Mindstorms exercise is the first piece of Part IA coursework, run early in Michaelmas Term (5 timetabled sessions in 2026-27; the 2022 preparation page places them in Weeks 1 and 2, so check this year's timetable). Working in a team, you design, build and program a small Lego system and present it at the end.

Aims (from the department's preparation page, last updated 2022)
- To give a first taste of real engineering system design and its practical difficulties, such as backlash in gears, structural rigidity and automatic control.
- At this stage you are expected to find ad hoc fixes for these problems; more disciplined methods come later in the course.
- To develop teamwork and communication skills.
- To learn the basics of Python, which is used to control the Lego system.

What you build
- A Lego system that demonstrates some aspect of engineering science, controlled by your own Python program.
- The preparation page is explicit that simple robots that just drive around, and are little more than toys, are not what is wanted.
- Ideas can come from the suggested projects, from things you have seen online, or from your own imagination.
- The components to get to know are the programmable brick, the motors, the sensors, the structural pieces (both studded and pin-jointed) and mechanisms such as gear trains.

Note: the preparation page was last updated in 2022 and refers to the Lego Mindstorms NXT kit, which may since have been replaced. Treat the kit, software and day-by-day schedule as possibly out of date and check the course's own pages or Moodle when you arrive.

Schedule (from the department's preparation page, last updated in 2022, so possibly out of date: check this year's timetable)
- Teams are allocated after departmental registration, only two days before the exercise starts, so you cannot plan with your team in advance.
- Week 1 Thursday, session 1: preliminary experiments. This session is highly structured and introduces the Python environment and the Lego sensors and actuators.
- Week 1 Friday, session 2: design and build.
- Week 2 Monday and Tuesday, sessions 3 and 4: design and build.
- Week 2 Wednesday: no session; prepare your presentation.
- Week 2 Thursday, session 5: presentations. There are prizes for the best systems.
- The 2026-27 coursework overview confirms 5 timetabled sessions in Michaelmas, of which 2 or 3 are in the afternoon.

Credit (2026-27 coursework and examination credit notice)
- Lego Mindstorms Project: 12 marks in total, qualifying level 10.
- 4 sessions at 2 marks each, given for prompt attendance and satisfactory work.
- An assessment marked on a 0–4 scale.
- So turning up on time to every session and producing satisfactory work is most of the credit.

How Part IA coursework counts (2026-27 credit notice)
- All Part IA coursework is for standard credit. Once you reach the satisfactory standard, your marks for an activity are capped at its qualifying level, so there is no reward for going beyond it.
- The qualifying marks for all Part IA coursework add up to 200. The coursework mark that counts is your raw total minus 100, so it is at most 100.
- That is added to the four written papers, each marked out of 200, giving 900 marks in all for Part IA.
- You must complete every activity satisfactorily to get the full qualifying mark. Missing, late or unsatisfactory work leaves a shortfall, and the Part IA guide says shortfalls are deducted from your Tripos total.
- If illness or grave cause stops you completing coursework, the notice says you can apply to the EAMC for an allowance; for missed sessions, follow the department's rules on rearranging coursework and extensions.
- Submitted work must be your own, and any use of AI tools must follow University and departmental guidance.

The department's preparation page recommends some light preparation before you arrive. None of it is assessed, but it makes the first sessions far more productive.

Recommended by the department (2022 preparation page)
- Watch some videos of Lego Mindstorms systems (the 2022 page suggests searching for "Lego NXT"; if the kit has changed, search for the current one) to get a feel for the common components and mechanisms.
- Read the material on the department's IA Lego website (linked from the preparation page), which covers the equipment, includes a tutorial on Lego gears and lists suggested projects.
- If you have Lego Technic at home, practise building with it.
- Start thinking about what system you would like to build: a suggested project, a variation of something you have seen online, or an original idea.

Useful background
- Python basics: variables, loops, if-statements and functions. Session 1 introduces the environment, but arriving able to write a simple loop saves time.
- Gears: with a driver gear of N₁ teeth meshing with a driven gear of N₂ teeth, the output turns at N₁/N₂ times the input speed, and the torque is ideally multiplied by N₂/N₁. A small gear driving a large one slows the output and increases its torque.
- Backlash: the small free play between meshing teeth. When the input reverses, the output does not move until the slack is taken up, which spoils precise positioning. Keeping gear trains short, or always approaching a target from the same direction, reduces its effect.
- Feedback: in open-loop control a command is sent with no check of the result; in closed-loop control a sensor measures the output and the difference from the target is used to correct the command.
- Rigidity: Lego structures flex. Triangulated bracing, rather than rectangles, stiffens a frame, an idea you will meet formally in 1P2 Structures.

On the day
- Agree roles early (building, programming, testing, presentation) but rotate so everyone learns Python.
- Build and test in small steps; get one sensor or motor working before combining them.
- Keep a record of what you tried and why it failed: it makes the presentation much stronger.
- Make sure your presentation explains the engineering science your system demonstrates, not just what it does.

cards.f: Language used to control the Lego system
What kind of system should you build?
cards.b: One that demonstrates some aspect of engineering science; not a simple robot that just drives around.
12 marks: 4 sessions × 2 marks (prompt attendance and satisfactory work) plus an assessment on a 0–4 scale. Qualifying level 10.
Free play between meshing gear teeth: when the input reverses, the output does not move until the slack is taken up, causing positioning errors.

cards.f: Speed and torque through a pair of gears
cards.b: Driver N₁ teeth, driven N₂ teeth: output speed = input × N₁/N₂; torque ideally × N₂/N₁ (ignoring friction losses).
Open-loop: a command is sent with no measurement of the result. Closed-loop: a sensor measures the output and the error is fed back to correct the command.

questions.q: An 8-tooth gear on a motor drives a 40-tooth gear. Ignoring friction, how do the output speed and torque compare with the motor's?
options: One fifth of the speed, five times the torque
Five times the speed, one fifth of the torque
One fifth of the speed, one fifth of the torque
The same speed, five times the torque
questions.why: The ratio is 40/8 = 5. The small driver turns the large gear more slowly (speed × 8/40 = 1/5), and with no losses power is conserved, so the torque rises by the same factor of 5. Five times the speed with one fifth of the torque has the ratio the wrong way round; one fifth of both would mean power was lost; the same speed with five times the torque ignores the speed change.
